templates.name: Sequential Sign-Off
templates.description: A durable sequential sign-off chain — pause-per-gate approvals with reminders, timeout escalation, and compensation on rejection.

steps.name: start
steps.description: Resolve the subject, the ordered approvers, and the escalation / ledger / reminder settings; initialise the chain state. An empty chain escalates.

steps.name: present
steps.description: Record the gate as pending and email the current approver, then pause until the approval signal (resumes at 'decide').

steps.name: decide
steps.description: Resume target — its input is the approval payload; approve advances to the next gate or finalises, reject compensates, timeout/no-response escalates, and any other resume is a reminder tick.

steps.name: remind
steps.description: Email a reminder to the current approver, then pause again on the same gate (resumes at 'decide').

steps.name: finalize
steps.description: The single irreversible action — reached only after every party approved; a dryRun guard makes it a no-op offline.

steps.name: compensate
steps.description: Saga rollback: someone rejected — notify everyone who already approved that the chain was cancelled.

steps.name: escalate
steps.description: Terminal branch: a gate went silent or timed out — escalate to a human channel.

templates.name: Personalized Cold Outreach
templates.description: Enrich a lead list, write a personalized first line for each prospect, verify deliverability, then drip follow-ups that stop the moment someone replies.

steps.name: enrich
steps.description: Resolve a real contact for each lead with Hunter — look up the named person, or surface a decision-maker when you only have the company.

steps.name: scrape
steps.description: Read each company's website for a few lines of context to personalize with.

steps.name: personalize
steps.description: Ask the live model to write one specific opener per prospect, falling back to a safe generic line when it returns nothing usable.

steps.name: verify
steps.description: Check each address for deliverability and drop the ones that would bounce before anything sends.

steps.name: launch
steps.description: Persist the campaign roster to a Postgres store the engine owns, then start the drip. A dry run stops here and returns the full plan without sending or persisting.

steps.name: send
steps.description: Deliver the current touch to everyone still active and log it, then pause at $0 until the drip interval elapses or a prospect replies.

steps.name: advance
steps.description: Wake on the reply-or-timeout, mark anyone who replied as done, then loop back for the next touch or end the run.

steps.name: done
steps.description: Return the campaign summary — who was enriched, how many were deliverable, what was sent, and who replied.

templates.name: Content Repurposing
templates.description: Turn one blog post or transcript into a tweet thread, LinkedIn post, newsletter, quote graphics, and a short clip — then email the whole pack.

steps.name: repurpose
steps.description: An LLM rewrites your source into every channel at once: the tweet thread, LinkedIn post, newsletter, pull-quotes, and a video script. If you set dryRun, it stops here and returns the copy.

steps.name: graphics
steps.description: Make one quote graphic per pull-quote, all at once, and save each one.

steps.name: clip
steps.description: Launch a video job that animates the first quote graphic into a short teaser clip, then pause until it finishes.

steps.name: collectClip
steps.description: Save the finished teaser clip.

steps.name: package
steps.description: Assemble the whole pack as one markdown document and upload it to file storage for a durable download link.

steps.name: deliver
steps.description: Email the pack to your recipient, or return it when no recipient is set. Ends the run with a summary of everything produced.

templates.name: Dependency Upgrade
templates.description: On a schedule, a coding agent bumps a repo's dependencies in a sandbox, runs the tests, and pushes only when the build is green.

steps.name: plan
steps.description: Resolves the repo and the install and test commands and checks the input; with no repo it stops right away.

steps.name: bump
steps.description: Launches a coding agent to bump the repo's dependencies in a sandbox, then pauses until the run finishes.

steps.name: verify
steps.description: Re-attaches that sandbox and runs the install and test suite there; a failed run or a red build is rejected.

steps.name: assess
steps.description: Asks a model to rate the upgrade's risk from the dependency diff, holding anything above your bar.

steps.name: publish
steps.description: Pushes the bumped branch from the sandbox and archives the triage report.

steps.name: held
steps.description: The build was green but the risk was too high, so it archives the report and waits for a human.

steps.name: rejected
steps.description: The coding run failed or the tests were red, so it archives the report and pushes nothing.

templates.name: Large Dataset Backfill
templates.description: Process a huge dataset in resumable chunks, checkpointing progress so the job survives restarts and picks up where it left off.

steps.name: plan
steps.description: Works out the job — dataset size, chunk size, and a stable job id — then resumes from a saved checkpoint if one exists for that id.

steps.name: process
steps.description: Process the current chunk, save its result and rewrite the checkpoint, then wait for the next heartbeat — or, running offline with nothing to fire one, loop straight to the next chunk. Finishes once the last chunk is done.

steps.name: finalize
steps.description: Writes a manifest of the run and returns a summary.

templates.name: Daily Error Digest
templates.description: Ingest errors by webhook or a scheduled pull, cluster and summarize them with an LLM, dedupe against a database, and email a daily digest.

steps.name: collect
steps.description: Gather the error batch — take it directly, GET it from a pull URL, or pause at $0 until a webhook pushes one via the errors.pushed signal.

steps.name: triage
steps.description: Hand the raw errors to an LLM to cluster them into distinct issues, each with a stable fingerprint, a severity, and an occurrence count.

steps.name: dedupe
steps.description: Look each fingerprint up in a Postgres store: never-seen ones are new, the rest are recurring, and their running totals are updated. Skipped on a dry run.

steps.name: digest
steps.description: Write a markdown digest — new issues first, recurring below — and email it. A dry run, or a run with no recipient, returns it without sending.

templates.name: Output Quality Check
templates.description: Score an output against your own rubric with an LLM judge, then branch to publish or revise on whether it clears a threshold.

steps.name: judge
steps.description: Build a judge prompt from your rubric, call the LLM (models.run), and parse a 0-to-1 score from the reply.

steps.name: gate
steps.description: Compare the score to your threshold. At or above goes to publish, below goes to revise. No LLM call here.

steps.name: publish
steps.description: The output cleared the threshold. Return the decision, score, threshold, and rationale.

steps.name: revise
steps.description: The output fell below the threshold. Return the decision, score, threshold, and rationale.

templates.name: Hello Agent
templates.description: The smallest working Sapiom agent — one step that returns a greeting, so you can confirm build, deploy, and run before adding a real capability.

steps.name: greet
steps.description: Read the optional name input and return a greeting, defaulting to "world" when none is given. This is the only step, and it ends the run.

templates.name: Approval Before Action
templates.description: An agent does the prep, then waits for a person to approve before it spends money or does anything it can't undo.

steps.name: parse
steps.description: Read the free-text request and pull out what's being asked and the criteria that should drive the choice (models.run).

steps.name: rank
steps.description: Score and order the candidates by how well they fit the criteria, not just price (models.run).

steps.name: notifyApprover
steps.description: Email the approver the ranked recommendation, then pause and wait for their decision — costing nothing while idle. With no approver set, stop at the gate with the shortlist instead of waiting forever.

steps.name: onDecision
steps.description: Read the approval reply: approve enters the offer loop, reject backs out, and no candidates escalates to a person.

steps.name: revert
steps.description: Rejected — back out to a safe state and finish, having committed nothing.

steps.name: offer
steps.description: Make a provisional, non-binding offer to the top-ranked candidate, then pause until they confirm (resumes at 'resolve').

steps.name: resolve
steps.description: Read the candidate's reply: accept commits, decline or timeout moves to the next candidate, and an exhausted list escalates.

steps.name: commit
steps.description: The one irreversible step — runs only after a human approved and a candidate accepted; a dry run makes it a no-op offline.

steps.name: pending
steps.description: No approver was set, so the run stops holding the ranked shortlist and the signal that continues it. Nothing was offered, and nothing was approved.

steps.name: escalate
steps.description: The ranked list ran out, or nobody could be contacted — hand off to a person.

templates.name: Meeting Notes to CRM
templates.description: Take a meeting transcript, pull out the contact, the CRM fields to update, and the action items, write them to a database, and email a summary.

steps.name: intake
steps.description: Takes the transcript — passed in directly, or, with webhook set, pauses at $0 until a note-taker pushes one via the transcript.ready signal.

steps.name: extract
steps.description: Hands the transcript to an LLM to pull the contact, the CRM fields to update, and the action items as structured JSON.

steps.name: upsert
steps.description: Writes to a Postgres CRM store: updates the contact's row without wiping unmentioned fields, and records each action item under a stable id. Skipped on a dry run.

steps.name: summary
steps.description: Writes a markdown recap — fields updated, action items new vs. already tracked — and emails it. A dry run, or a run with no recipient, returns it without sending.

templates.name: Company News Roundup
templates.description: Search the web for a company's recent news, then publish a dated, illustrated roundup page to a small website for that company.

steps.name: search
steps.description: Search the web for the company's news from the last week. If nothing comes back, stop early and report no news instead of publishing.

steps.name: select
steps.description: Ask an LLM to pick the three-to-five most relevant articles and write a plain-language summary and an image prompt for each.

steps.name: illustrate
steps.description: Generate one image per selected article and save each to storage; an article whose image fails degrades to a text-only card.

steps.name: publish
steps.description: Save the dated page, rebuild the company's site from storage in a sandbox, and deploy it — returning the live site and page URLs.

templates.name: Newsletter Autopilot
templates.description: On a weekly schedule, it researches a niche, writes and illustrates the issue, and emails it to your subscriber list.

steps.name: search
steps.description: Search the web for the niche and collect candidate sources.

steps.name: scrape
steps.description: Read the top candidates for their full article text, keeping just the snippet when a page won't load.

steps.name: write
steps.description: Hand the sources to an LLM to curate them and write this week's issue: a subject, a body that cites each source, and a header-image prompt.

steps.name: header
steps.description: Generate a header image for the issue; if none comes back, the issue still goes out without it.

steps.name: deliver
steps.description: Email each subscriber their own copy; a dry run, or a run with no subscribers set, returns the issue without sending.

templates.name: Ask Your Database
templates.description: Deploy a live endpoint that turns a plain-English question into a read-only SQL query and returns the answer.

steps.name: validate
steps.description: Checks the input (a database handle or connection string) and resolves config.

steps.name: resolve
steps.description: Reads the target Postgres connection string from a Sapiom database handle to inject into the endpoint.

steps.name: plan
steps.description: Previews the pipeline: translates the sample question into SQL with an LLM.

steps.name: guard
steps.description: Applies the read-only guardrail to the sample SQL; anything that isn't a single read-only statement is rejected.

steps.name: deploy
steps.description: Write the endpoint server into a sandbox and expose it at a stable URL, injecting DATABASE_URL and the endpoint's own API key. With no key, nothing is deployed.

steps.name: endpoint_skipped
steps.description: The endpoint needs an API key of its own to translate each request; without one nothing is deployed, and the run returns the translated, guarded SQL instead of a URL that cannot answer.

steps.name: deployed
steps.description: The endpoint is live — returns its URL and the previewed sample query.

steps.name: deploy_failed
steps.description: The deploy failed — surfaces the deployPreview logs.

steps.name: rejected
steps.description: Input or the sample SQL failed the guardrail; nothing was deployed.

templates.name: Personalized Media Per Lead
templates.description: Read a table of leads and, per row, generate a personalized image or short clip, store it, and email each person a link — on a schedule.

steps.name: fetch
steps.description: Read up to `limit` recipient rows from a database table, seeding a demo table on the first run. If you set dryRun, it stops here and returns the rows and their prompts.

steps.name: renderImages
steps.description: For the image medium: make one personalized image per row, all at once, and save each.

steps.name: renderClip
steps.description: For the video medium: launch a short clip for one row, then pause until it finishes.

steps.name: collectClip
steps.description: Save the finished clip, then loop back for the next row, or move on once every row is done.

steps.name: deliver
steps.description: Email each recipient a link to their own asset; a dry run generates and sends nothing.

templates.name: PR Review Bot
templates.description: When a pull request opens, a coding agent reviews the code and flags missing tests, then posts the review to your email or Slack.

steps.name: watch
steps.description: Register with the webhook source and pause until a PR opens — costing nothing while idle. With no source configured, review the built-in sample PR instead of waiting forever.

steps.name: review
steps.description: Wakes when a PR opens; its input is the PR payload. A coding agent checks the code out and analyzes the diff, flagging changes that lack tests.

steps.name: assess
steps.description: A model turns the coding agent's raw findings into a structured review — a verdict, a summary, and the list of missing tests.

steps.name: reportEmail
steps.description: Emails the review to the configured recipient.

steps.name: reportSlack
steps.description: Post the review to the configured channel with your Slack bot token. Without one, the review is returned in the run's output and nothing is posted.

steps.name: posted
steps.description: Return the result — the channel used and the verdict.

steps.name: failed
steps.description: The send errored; return the error.

templates.name: Preview Uptime Monitor
templates.description: A cron heartbeat that checks a sandbox preview and, when it has gone down, redeploys it for you — no human needed.

steps.name: check
steps.description: Fetch the preview's health path and send it on to heal only when the app is actually down. With no target given, provision one first.

steps.name: provision
steps.description: With no target given, create a small sandbox with a trivial health server in it, so the heal step has a real app to relaunch.

steps.name: healthy
steps.description: The app is already serving, so there's nothing to do. The run ends here.

steps.name: heal
steps.description: Re-attach the sandbox and redeploy the code already uploaded there, restarting it at the same URL. First assembles the startup env, adding a DATABASE_URL from a Postgres handle and any declared secrets the platform injected.

steps.name: healed
steps.description: The relaunch worked. Reports the URL and status.

steps.name: heal_failed
steps.description: The relaunch didn't work. Reports the deploy logs so you can see why.

templates.name: Client Proposal Generator
templates.description: Draft a client proposal from a request, render it to a PDF, then wait for a person to approve it before it emails the client.

steps.name: draft
steps.description: An LLM turns the request into a structured proposal — title, summary, scope, and priced line items — then the totals are computed in code, not trusted from the model.

steps.name: render
steps.description: Spin up a sandbox, lay the proposal out as a PDF with a small Node script, save the file to storage, then tear the sandbox down.

steps.name: review
steps.description: Email the approver a summary and the PDF link, then pause and wait for their decision — costing nothing while idle. With no approver set, stop at the gate with the drafted proposal instead of waiting forever.

steps.name: onDecision
steps.description: Read the approval reply: approve emails the client, anything else stops safely with nothing sent.

steps.name: send
steps.description: The one outward step — email the approved proposal to the client. A dry run skips the send.

steps.name: pending
steps.description: No approver was set, so the run stops holding the drafted proposal and the signal that continues it. Nothing was sent, and nothing was approved.

steps.name: rejected
steps.description: Rejected at review — nothing goes to the client, and the draft PDF stays on file.

templates.name: Research Micro-Site
templates.description: Research a topic across the web, then build and deploy a shareable live report site — not just a document.

steps.name: search
steps.description: Take the topic and run one web search for candidate sources.

steps.name: scrape
steps.description: Read the top candidates for their full article text, keeping just the snippet when a page won't load.

steps.name: synthesize
steps.description: Hand the sources to an LLM to write a structured, cited report. A dry run — or a report too empty to build a site from — stops here and returns the report.

steps.name: build
steps.description: Launch a coding agent to build a self-contained static site from the report, then pause until it finishes — costing nothing while it works.

steps.name: publish
steps.description: Re-attach the coding agent's sandbox and deploy the site to a stable public URL.

steps.name: mapDomain
steps.description: If a domain you own is configured, point a subdomain at the live site with a free CNAME; otherwise this is skipped.

steps.name: live
steps.description: Return the live URL, the custom URL when one was mapped, the report title, and the sources.

steps.name: failed
steps.description: The build or the deploy failed; return the stage and the logs.

steps.name: drafted
steps.description: The dry-run off-ramp: the report was computed but nothing was built or deployed.

templates.name: Scene to Video
templates.description: Turn one scene description into a short, multi-shot video with a consistent style.

steps.name: decompose
steps.description: An LLM turns your scene into a style guide and an ordered shot list. If you set dryRun, it stops here and returns the plan.

steps.name: keyframes
steps.description: Make one keyframe image per shot, all at once, and save each one.

steps.name: animate
steps.description: Launch a video job that animates one keyframe into a clip, then pause until it finishes.

steps.name: collect
steps.description: Save the finished clip, then loop back for the next shot, or move on once every clip is in.

steps.name: stitch
steps.description: Join the clips into one video with a merge job, then pause until it's ready.

steps.name: finalize
steps.description: Return the stitched video's file id and download link.

templates.name: Signed Compliance Audit
templates.description: On a schedule, it audits your resources against a policy, waits for a person to sign off, then archives the signed attestation.

steps.name: collect
steps.description: Read the current state of each resource with a scrape, keeping the error as missing evidence when a page won't load.

steps.name: audit
steps.description: Hand the collected state and your policy to an LLM to produce a verdict and one evidence-cited check per requirement.

steps.name: review
steps.description: Hold the drafted attestation and pause for a human sign-off — costing nothing while idle. With no signer set, stop at the gate with the draft instead of waiting forever.

steps.name: onSignoff
steps.description: Read the sign-off reply: an explicit approve archives the attestation, anything else backs out with nothing filed.

steps.name: archive
steps.description: Write the signed attestation to durable file storage and return its file id and download link; a dry run skips the upload.

steps.name: pending
steps.description: No signer was set, so the run stops holding a DRAFT attestation. Nothing was signed, filed, or archived.

steps.name: rejected
steps.description: Sign-off was declined — return the audit findings, having archived nothing.

templates.name: Scheduled Metrics Report
templates.description: On a schedule, query a database, write the narrative and render charts, then email the insight report.

steps.name: snapshot
steps.description: Runs the read-only queries against the database and normalizes each result into a metric — a labeled series or a scalar KPI.

steps.name: narrate
steps.description: Hands the metrics to a model to write a short markdown report — a summary, insights that cite the numbers, and what to watch.

steps.name: chart
steps.description: Renders the series into an SVG bar chart inside a sandbox, hosts it in file storage, and takes a shareable link.

steps.name: deliver
steps.description: Emails the report — narrative, chart link, and a metrics table. A dry run or a missing recipient returns it as a preview instead.

templates.name: Scheduled Research Brief
templates.description: On a schedule, it researches a topic and emails you a short, sourced brief.

steps.name: search
steps.description: Search the web for the topic and collect candidate sources.

steps.name: scrape
steps.description: Read the top candidates for their full article text, keeping just the snippet when a page won't load.

steps.name: curate
steps.description: Hand the sources to an LLM to rank them, drop the weak ones, and write a short brief that cites each one.

steps.name: deliver
steps.description: Email the brief to your recipient; a dry run, or a run with no recipient set, returns it without sending.

templates.name: Slack Notifier
templates.description: Post a message to Slack with your own bot token — the starter for wiring up any external API.

steps.name: validate
steps.description: Check the message, pick the auth mode (bot or webhook), and resolve the target channel.

steps.name: post
steps.description: Post the message to Slack with your bot token. Without one, the message is returned in the run's output and nothing is posted.

steps.name: posted
steps.description: Return the result — for bot mode, the channel and the message timestamp.

steps.name: failed
steps.description: The Slack call errored; return the error.

steps.name: rejected
steps.description: The input didn't pass validation, so nothing was posted.

templates.name: Workflow Fleet Monitor
templates.description: Watches a fleet of workflows, spots which member is off cadence, and launches it — with a model that may only pick from a fixed list of safe moves.

steps.name: scan
steps.description: Reads the event log and works out which members are off cadence — missed today, overdue, or launched with no result.

steps.name: assess
steps.description: Hands those situations to a model that may only pick a move from a fixed list, then re-checks its answer in code.

steps.name: actuate
steps.description: Runs the plan behind guardrails, launching each due member as a child workflow and recording each launch.

steps.name: report
steps.description: Posts a short briefing to a Slack channel, records the run, and advances its place in the log.

templates.name: Slow Job Callback
templates.description: Start a slow external job, pause until a webhook calls back, then summarize the result and decide whether to accept it.

steps.name: kickoff
steps.description: Register the resume contract with the external job and pause until it calls back — costing nothing while idle. With no register URL, no job was started, so it decides on an empty payload rather than waiting forever.

steps.name: decide
steps.description: Wakes when the callback arrives; its input is the callback payload. A model summarizes the result and picks accept or reject.

steps.name: accept
steps.description: Ends the run — the callback result looked complete and usable.

steps.name: reject
steps.description: Ends the run — the callback result failed or looked wrong.

templates.name: Web Research Digest
templates.description: Search the web for a topic and get back a short, sourced digest.

steps.name: search
steps.description: Take the topic and run one web search, returning a synthesized answer and ranked results.

steps.name: summarize
steps.description: Format that answer and its source links into a markdown digest, in the run and with no model call.
